title: HTTP response splitting and header-value injection
attackSurface: Attacker-controlled text copied into an HTTP response header value

references.note: Node.js writeHead reason CRLF response-splitting vulnerability

hostile.title: CRLF Set-Cookie injection
hostile.why: Classic response splitting that adds a attacker-controlled cookie header

hostile.title: CRLF Location injection
hostile.why: Injected redirect header in a split response

hostile.title: LF-only header split
hostile.why: Bare line feed accepted by some broken intermediaries

hostile.title: CR-only header split
hostile.why: Carriage return alone is still a line-control injection primitive

hostile.title: Response body splitting
hostile.why: Double line break attempts to move attacker content into the response body

hostile.title: NUL truncation primitive
hostile.why: NUL bytes can create parser differentials in downstream native code

hostile.title: Unicode line separator
hostile.why: Line-separator characters must not survive into header output

hostile.title: DEL control injection
hostile.why: DEL and other control characters are outside safe HTTP field-value grammar

benign.title: Plain cache value
benign.why: Ordinary Cache-Control value with a comma

benign.title: Content type with parameters
benign.why: Semicolon parameters are valid header syntax

benign.title: Latin-1 visible text
benign.why: Visible Latin-1 text is not a control injection

benign.title: CSP nonce source
benign.why: Single quotes and spaces are normal CSP text
